question: What is the main sign of diabetes mellitus?
explanation: Diabetes is characterized by high blood glucose levels resulting from insulin defects. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: Why is early detection of diabetes by nurses so important?

options.A: It completely cures the underlying genetic defect
options.B: It reverses complete pancreatic cell destruction
options.C: It stops disease progression and prevents multi-organ damage
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medication

explanation: Early identification allows prompt intervention, reducing the risk of long-term complications. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: What causes the body to stop making insulin in Type 1 diabetes?
explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system attacks and destroys insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: Type 2 diabetes is mainly caused by which of these?

options.A: Insulin resistance and relative secretory defect
options.B: Excessive destruction of circulating insulin molecules
options.C: Complete autoimmune destruction of the pancreas
options.D: Temporary glucose intolerance during pregnancy only

explanation: The body's cells fail to respond properly to insulin, and the pancreas eventually fails to compensate adequately. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: Why do patients with uncontrolled diabetes pass urine very frequently?

options.A: Osmotic diuresis from excess renal glucose
options.B: Increased water intake from heavy exercise
options.C: Rapid bacterial infection in the bladder

explanation: High blood sugar overflows into the urine, pulling water along with it and causing frequent urination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why do untreated diabetic patients eat a lot yet still lose weight?

options.A: The digestive tract absorbs nutrients much faster than normal
options.B: Insulin excess drives the storage of all available calories
options.C: Cells starve for glucose, forcing the body to burn fat and muscle
options.D: Kidneys excrete protein instead of breaking it down for energy

explanation: Without insulin to let glucose in, cells lack energy, triggering hunger while the body consumes its own tissues. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which test checks blood sugar control over the past three months?
explanation: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose levels over the preceding two to three months. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h4)

question: What is a major problem when storing blood glucose test strips in warm, humid climates?

options.A: Moisture improves the chemical accuracy of the testing pads
options.B: High humidity can damage strips and cause false readings
options.C: Sunlight exposure increases the battery life of glucometers
options.D: Cold temperatures will freeze the electronic components

explanation: Test strips are sensitive to moisture and heat, which degrade the reagents and yield inaccurate results. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h4)

question: How does metformin mainly work to treat Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Reducing hepatic glucose production and improving sensitivity
options.B: Stimulating immediate release of glucagon from the liver
options.C: Destroying autoantibodies attacking pancreatic beta cells
options.D: Increasing renal excretion of proteins and electrolytes

explanation: Metformin helps lower blood sugar by decreasing liver glucose output and making muscle cells more responsive to insulin. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: Why must patients regularly change their insulin injection sites?

options.A: To keep the skin surface clean and prevent bacterial infection
options.B: To stop the muscles underneath from becoming completely paralyzed
options.C: To prevent lumpy fat deposits and ensure predictable absorption
options.D: To make the needle sharper for subsequent daily injections

explanation: Injecting in the same spot repeatedly causes lipodystrophy, which erraticizes insulin absorption. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: How does regular exercise help someone with diabetes?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any diet changes
options.B: It permanently cures pancreatic beta cell loss
options.C: It stops the liver from storing excess glycogen

explanation: Exercise helps muscle cells use glucose more effectively without requiring as much insulin. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why is local culture and food important when planning diabetes diets in Nigeria?

options.A: Traditional dishes have zero carbohydrate content by nature
options.B: Dietary advice must incorporate locally available, affordable foods
options.C: Local staples prevent the development of diabetic neuropathy
options.D: Patients will refuse treatment if imported foods are recommended

explanation: Meal plans succeed only when they align with what patients can realistically access and afford within their communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a small blood vessel (microvascular) complication of diabetes?
explanation: Coronary artery disease is classified as a macrovascular complication, affecting large blood vessels rather than tiny capillaries. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h7)

question: Why are regular foot checks very important for diabetic patients?

options.A: Blood flow to the lower limbs increases rapidly every night
options.B: Fungal infections of the skin destroy all nerve endings permanently
options.C: Neuropathy reduces sensation, allowing injuries to go unnoticed and ulcerate
options.D: Sweat gland failure causes complete dryness of the toenails

explanation: Loss of protective sensation means patients cannot feel cuts or pressure sores, which can quickly lead to severe ulcers and gangrene. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is a major benefit of support groups for people living with diabetes?

options.A: They replace the need for professional laboratory checkups
options.B: They supply free insulin injections for life
options.C: They cure the metabolic disorder completely
options.D: They reduce stigma and encourage peer learning

explanation: Support groups provide shared experiences, emotional encouragement, and practical coping strategies for daily disease management. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h8)

question: What is the most important thing to teach a patient who is just starting insulin therapy?

options.B: Methods to completely reverse beta cell destruction
options.C: How to store medication in direct tropical sunlight
options.D: Techniques for avoiding all forms of physical activity

explanation: Patients must be able to identify and quickly treat low blood sugar, which is a dangerous potential side effect of insulin therapy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h8)
